close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2 with doc-only treatment: added module-level rustdoc above the 22 sloppy fields explaining that values MUST be JSON objects per RFC 9553 sub-object definitions, the wire type accepts any JSON shape, and the handler layer is responsible for rejecting non-object values with invalidProperties per RFC 8620 §5.3. Adding serde-level validation would break partial responses and PatchObject semantics, and diverge from the workspace canonical pattern (Calendars/Tasks).
description:
ContactCard's 22 `Option<serde_json::Value>` fields accept any JSON value
shape at serde level — string, number, array, bool, null, object. None
of the doc comments document the wire-format constraint that these MUST
be JSON objects (per RFC 9553 sub-object definitions).

Failure mode:

```rust
let mut card = ContactCard::default();
card.name   = Some(serde_json::json!("just a string"));     // wrong shape
card.emails = Some(serde_json::json!([1, 2, 3]));            // wrong shape
let wire = serde_json::to_string(&card).unwrap();
// Round-trips cleanly. Server stores it. Server returns it.

// Downstream client (or test) tries typed access:
let name: Name = serde_json::from_value(card.name.unwrap()).unwrap();
//     ^^^^^ panics at deserialize: Name expects {components, full, ...}
```

A caller submitting a ContactCard/set with `"name": "Joe"` produces a
wire-format violation of RFC 9553, but the server is forced to either:

1. Accept and re-serve (corrupt wire data propagates indefinitely)
2. Validate at the deserialize boundary with a custom adapter
3. Validate at use-site with from_value, panic, or return an
   Internal Server Error

The doc comment for each sloppy field should at minimum say "MUST be
a JSON object per RFC 9553 §<section>; primitives and arrays will
round-trip but will fail downstream typed access."

A stronger fix: replace `Option<serde_json::Value>` with
`Option<serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>>`. Wire format
identical for valid input; rejects primitive/array input at deserialize
boundary; preserves sloppy semantics inside the object.

Note: `localizations` already uses the typed shape
`Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>` (good — wire-byte-identical via
#[serde(transparent)] on PatchObject). The same upgrade should be
considered for the 22 remaining sloppy fields.

Cross-reference:
- AGENTS.md §"Sloppy-Value pattern" — current policy
- card.rs:86-178 — the 22 affected fields
- card.rs:161 — localizations as the good precedent
title: ContactCard sloppy fields accept any JSON value type; primitives/arrays round-trip but break typed downstream access
